attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
2	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
3	import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';

5	const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
6	export const ROOT = resolve(__dirname, '..');
7	
8	/** 读取并规范化 config.json */
9	export function loadConfig() {
10	  const raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(ROOT, 'config.json'), 'utf8'));
11	  return {
12	    // 告警目标群 webhook：支持单个字符串或数组（多个群同发）。兼容旧字段 feishuWebhook。
13	    feishuWebhooks: (Array.isArray(raw.feishuWebhooks)
14	      ? raw.feishuWebhooks
15	      : [raw.feishuWebhooks ?? raw.feishuWebhook ?? ''])
16	      .map((s) => String(s || '').trim()).filter(Boolean),
17	    feishuSecret: raw.feishuSecret || '',
18	    intervalMinutes: Number(raw.intervalMinutes) || 15,
19	    stores: raw.stores || 'all',
20	    storeList: Array.isArray(raw.storeList) ? raw.storeList : [],
21	    alerts: {
22	      onSaleDrop: raw.alerts?.onSaleDrop !== false,
23	      trafficAnomaly: raw.alerts?.trafficAnomaly !== false,
24	      // 登录过期/连续监测失败时发飞书提醒，避免登录态失效后静默死掉没人知道
25	      loginExpiry: raw.alerts?.loginExpiry !== false,
26	    },
27	    // 连续失败达到该轮次才发登录过期告警（默认 2 轮 ≈ 30 分钟，滤掉偶发抖动）
28	    loginAlertAfterRounds: Number(raw.loginAlertAfterRounds) || 2,
29	    // 仍未恢复时每隔多少轮再提醒一次（默认 16 轮 ≈ 4 小时，避免刷屏）
30	    loginRealertRounds: Number(raw.loginRealertRounds) || 16,
31	    headless: raw.headless === true,
32	    // 代理：config.proxy 若为字符串（含空串）则以它为准——空串 = 强制直连，
33	    // 不再回落系统 HTTPS_PROXY（实测本机 7897 代理会频繁 ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED，直连反而稳）。
34	    // 仅当 config.json 完全没有 proxy 字段时才跟随系统环境变量。
35	    proxy: typeof raw.proxy === 'string' ? raw.proxy : (process.env.HTTPS_PROXY || process.env.HTTP_PROXY || ''),
36	    loginUrl: raw.loginUrl || 'https://agentseller.temu.com/goods/list',
37	    goodsListUrl: raw.goodsListUrl || 'https://agentseller.temu.com/goods/list',
38	    userDataDir: resolve(ROOT, raw.userDataDir || './.userdata'),
39	    // 浏览器 channel：默认 'chrome' = 用系统真实 Chrome（指纹与真人一致，最不易被风控识别）。
40	    // 设为 '' 或 'chromium' 则回落 Playwright 内置 Chromium。
41	    channel: raw.channel === '' ? '' : (raw.channel || 'chrome'),
42	    // 可选：显式指定 chrome.exe 路径，优先级高于 channel。
43	    executablePath: raw.executablePath || '',

content.text:
Here is the complete report on the monitor's logger, state persistence, and file management strategy.

---

## 1. Full Logger Implementation

**File:** `E:\project\temu\temu-monitor\src\logger.js` (34 lines)

The logger is minimalist. It is an ES module that:

1. **Resolves the log directory and file** in module-level init code:
   - `LOG_DIR` = `<ROOT>/data` (where `ROOT` is `resolve(__dirname, '..')` from `config.js`, i.e., the project root).
   - The `data/` directory is lazily created with `mkdirSync(LOG_DIR, { recursive: true })` inside a silent `try/catch`.
   - `LOG_FILE` = `data/monitor.log`.

2. **Formats timestamps** via a local `ts()` helper:
   ```js
   new Date().toISOString().replace('T', ' ').slice(0, 19)
   ```
   This produces strings like `2026-07-20 14:30:45` (local time, 19 characters, space-separated instead of ISO's `T`).

3. **Serializes log arguments** via a `fmt(a)` helper:
   - Strings pass through unchanged.
   - `Error` instances use `stack` or `message`.
   - Everything else is `JSON.stringify(a)`, falling back to `String(a)`.

4. **Writes each log line** via the private `write(level, args)` function:
   ```js
   const line = `[${ts()}] [${level}] ${args.map(fmt).join(' ')}`;
   ```
   - Console output: `console.error(line)` for ERROR level, `console.log(line)` for all others.
   - File output: `appendFileSync(LOG_FILE, line + '\n')` wrapped in a silent `try/catch` -- **write errors are discarded without any indication**.

### Public API

The module exports a single `log` object with three methods:

| Method | Signature | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| `log.info(...args)` | variadic `(...a) => write('INFO', a)` | Informational messages |
| `log.warn(...args)` | variadic `(...a) => write('WARN', a)` | Warnings |
| `log.error(...args)` | variadic `(...a) => write('ERROR', a)` | Errors (also printed to stderr) |

### Log Format

```
[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] [LEVEL] <serialized arguments joined by space>
```

Example (hypothetical from the patterns used in `monitor.js`):
```
[2026-07-20 14:30:45] [INFO] 在售数量读自 countStatus 接口：142
[2026-07-20 14:31:02] [WARN] 未找到「商品流量待关注」快速筛选 chip。
[2026-07-20 14:35:10] [ERROR] 店铺「Store1」监测出错：net::ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED
```

### Consumer modules (logger is imported by every source file)

All 9 source files under `src/` import the logger:
`stores.js`, `run.js`, `feishu.js`, `calibrate.js`, `probe.js`, `monitor.js`, `cli.js`, `browser.js`, `popups.js`

A total of 69 `log.info/warn/error` call sites exist across those files, making the logger a central cross-cutting concern.

---

## 2. State Persistence (`state.js`)

**File:** `E:\project\temu\temu-monitor\src\state.js`

State is persisted as a plain JSON file at `<ROOT>/data/state.json` using two synchronous functions:

```js
export function loadState() {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(STATE_FILE, 'utf8'));
  } catch {
    return { stores: {} };
  }
}

export function saveState(state) {
  mkdirSync(resolve(ROOT, 'data'), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(STATE_FILE, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2), 'utf8');
}
```

Key characteristics:
- **Full read/write on every cycle** -- no incremental updates, no append-only journal.
- **No atomic write** -- a crash during `writeFileSync` leaves the file corrupted or half-written.
- **No backup** -- the previous state is overwritten in place.
- **Default fallback**: `{ stores: {} }` when the file is missing or unparseable.
- **Pretty-printed** with 2-space indentation (`JSON.stringify(state, null, 2)`).
- **Same directory as logs** -- shares the `data/` directory with `monitor.log`.
- **No locking, no concurrency control** (single-process Node.js, so this is not needed).
- The state stores per-store snapshots for diff-based alerting via the `diffStore()` function, which compares `onSaleCount`, `trafficWatchCount`, and `trafficDeclineExists` between rounds.

---

## 3. Log Rotation / File Management: NONE

After thoroughly searching every `.js` and `.mjs` file in the project (excluding `node_modules/`), there is **zero code** for:

- Log rotation (rename old log, start new one)
- Log truncation (keep only last N bytes/lines)
- Size limits (e.g., stop writing after 10 MB)
- Archival or compression
- Cleanup or pruning
- Any reference to `LOG_FILE`, `monitor.log`, file size, or disk usage outside of `logger.js` itself

The grep for `rotation|truncat|size|cleanup|prune|archive|maxFile|maxSize|MAX_LOG|delete.*log|remove.*log` across all project `.js` and `.mjs` files (excluding `node_modules/`) returned **no hits** in application code.

---

## 4. How the Monitor Handles Log File Growth

**It does not handle it.** The log file `data/monitor.log` grows unbounded for the lifetime of the process. Specifically:

- Every call to `log.info/warn/error` appends one line via `appendFileSync`.
- With a 15-minute monitoring interval (from `config.json` default), a typical run produces 5--15 log lines per cycle.
- Over weeks or months of continuous `npm start`, the file grows proportionally with no mechanism to cap it.
- Disk space is the only limit. Once the disk fills, the `catch {}` in `write()` silently swallows the `appendFileSync` error, meaning **the process loses all subsequent log writes without any alert**.
- The console output continues working even after the file write fails, creating a misleading appearance of normal operation.

This is a deliberate tradeoff for a personal monitoring tool -- the simplicity of append-only without rotation avoids complexity, and the data volume is small enough that disk exhaustion is unlikely in practice.

---

## 5. Patterns Adaptable for a Chrome Extension Context

The current logger is purpose-built for a Node.js process. Adapting it to a Chrome extension would require structural changes. Here are the pain points and what could be adapted or replaced:

### What cannot be directly ported

| Pattern | Node.js | Chrome Extension equivalent |
|---------|---------|-----------------------------|
| `appendFileSync` to a log file | Filesystem write | `chrome.storage.local.set()` or IndexedDB |
| `console.log / console.error` | Stdout/stderr | Same, works in service worker / popup / devtools |
| `mkdirSync` for directory creation | Filesystem | Not needed; storage APIs auto-initialize |
| `Date().toISOString()` | Node global | Still available via `Date` |
| Unlimited file growth | Disk is abundant | `chrome.storage.local` has a hard **10 MB limit** (Manifest V3); IndexedDB has a soft quota (~60% of disk) |

### Patterns worth adapting

1. **The three-level API (`info/warn/error`)** maps cleanly to Chrome extension needs -- the same interface can be kept and consumers do not need to change.

2. **Timestamp format** is portable -- `new Date().toISOString().replace('T', ' ').slice(0, 19)` works identically in extension contexts.

3. **The `fmt()` serializer** for Error stacks and JSON needs no changes.

4. **The silent error-catch around writes** should become **structured**, not hidden. In an extension, a `chrome.storage.local.set` failure could be due to the 10 MB quota being exhausted or `.set` calls happening during service worker shutdown (where they would be silently dropped). Either case warrants a retry or a callback to surface the failure.

### Critical additions needed for Chrome extensions

- **Size-aware storage**: Since `chrome.storage.local` has a 10 MB cap, the logger must either:
  - Use a **ring buffer** of the last N entries (e.g., keep only the last 500 log lines).
  - Use **IndexedDB** for larger persistent logs with pagination/cursor-based reads.
  - Use `chrome.storage.session` for ephemeral, current-session-only logs (cleared when the browser closes).

- **Storage key structure**: Instead of a file, logs should be stored under a namespaced key like `logs` in chrome.storage.local, with each entry stored as an object `{ ts, level, message }` rather than a continuously appended string.

- **Batch writes**: The current `appendFileSync` is called per-line. In an extension, batching multiple log entries into a single `.set()` call is more efficient and less likely to hit write throttling.

- **Export mechanism**: A file-based log is trivially accessible. In an extension, consider providing an "Export Logs" button that serializes stored entries to a downloadable text file via a Blob URL or `chrome.downloads.download`.

- **Quota awareness**: Periodically check `chrome.storage.local.getBytesInUse(null)` and trim oldest entries when approaching the limit, replacing the current strategy of silently ignoring write errors.

### Summary table of recommended adaptations

| Concern | Current approach | Recommended Chrome Extension approach |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------------------|
| Storage medium | `appendFileSync` to disk file | `chrome.storage.local` or IndexedDB |
| Growth control | None (unbounded) | Ring buffer (keep last N entries) or capped at ~8 MB |
| Write errors | Silently swallowed | Log to console, surface via `chrome.runtime.lastError` |
| API surface | `log.info/warn/error` | Keep identical API |
| Log format | `[ts] [LEVEL] args` | Store as structured `{ ts, level, msg }` objects |
| Quota monitoring | Not needed | Periodic `getBytesInUse` check with auto-trim |
| Export | Direct file access | Download via Blob + `chrome.downloads` API |
